rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭayyibāt are naturally beneficial, moderate, and wholesome; impure things are naturally harmful, and directives reflect those qualities.
rows.anchor: because of their nature and effect on human beings are beneficial, moderate and wholesome.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Different degrees of purity can make one thing prohibited and another merely undesirable.
rows.anchor: the degree of a directive may change regarding two things: one would be prohibited and the other undesirable.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thing not intrinsically impure can become so through an external condition, such as idolatrous sacrifice, gambling, or hunting during iḥrām.
rows.anchor: something extrinsic to it makes it impure. For example, an animal sacrificed in the name of some deity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purity and prohibition have a natural, logical, or moral basis; treating them as relative between peoples is scepticism.
rows.anchor: To regard something to be prohibited for one nation and allowed for the other is mere scepticism.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The category of bahīmat al-anʿām includes wild non-domesticated herbivores but excludes predators.
rows.anchor: are not domesticated, but are still subsumed under the category of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Predators are prohibited, as are carrion, swine, poured blood, and animals sacrificed to other deities because of their apparent or logical impurity.
rows.anchor: Thus the Prophet (sws) regarded predators to be prohibited. Similar is the case of carrion, swine, blood poured forth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same purity test applies to birds, sea animals, insects, and vegetables; predatory birds and alcohol are prohibited for impurity.
rows.anchor: alcohol prepared from everything will be prohibited because it has logical and moral impurity.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists differ over whether some animals are predators and whether some things are impure, given the many kinds of animals.
rows.anchor: there can be a difference of opinion in many of these. Thus such difference of opinion does exist among our jurists

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi finds the Ḥanafī jurists most aligned with Qur'anic principles; in disputed cases one may avoid doubtful things but must not condemn those who differ.
rows.anchor: the views of the Hanifite jurists hold the greatest harmony with the Qur’ ānic principles

rows.speaker: the Prophet (sws)
rows.claim: The Prophet's not eating lizard, as reported in narratives, is Islahi's model for handling doubtful cases.
rows.anchor: Prophet (sws) regarding not eating of the lizard mentioned in narratives gives us the best guidance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects as illogical and wrongly attributed the report that some Companions considered only the four previously listed items forbidden.
rows.anchor: This view does is not correct in any sense and it has been wrongly ascribed to them by some narrators.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He suggests they may instead have meant that Abraham's religion forbade only four quadruped animals, a claim true in its particular context.
rows.anchor: in the religion of Abraham (sws) only four things among quadruped animals are forbidden.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters' claim that God willed their polytheism is foolish: freedom to act does not make an act correct or divinely sanctioned.
rows.anchor: If people have the freedom to express certain views and do certain deeds, this does not mean that these views and deeds are correct.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples used the same excuse and were punished; the Prophet is told to leave these stubborn people to themselves.
rows.anchor: Prior to them, their predecessors also adopted this attitude and were ultimately punished for this by God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to reject their unsupported conjecture as insufficient knowledge.
rows.anchor: You are merely following conjecture and only make speculations.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an demands either eyewitness knowledge or a natural or intellectual basis for a claim; it cites Joseph 12:26–28 as an example and asks the idolaters for both kinds of proof.
rows.anchor: logical evidence can only be presented on two bases: personal observation or knowledge and some natural or intellectual ground

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's conclusive argument is delivered through reasoning and the messenger; God does not compel guidance, since people are free to accept or reject it.
rows.anchor: He provides guidance through arguments and reasoning and has given people the freedom to choose or reject it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the witnesses testify to a prohibition, the Prophet must not join their testimony or follow their desires; unsupported innovations arise from whims.
rows.anchor: Their innovations are signified by the word “desires.” This is because something that does not have any logical or scriptural justification

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters' denial of revelations, denial of the Hereafter, and polytheism show such rebellion that their desires have no sound destination.
rows.anchor: who are so rebellious that neither God or His verses nor the hereafter have any value before them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses detail Abraham's religion and expose the Quraysh's neglect of its duties to God and creatures while claiming adherence through invented food taboos; their first violation is polytheism.
rows.anchor: These verses state the real religion of Abraham (sws) in detail.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage states some duties positively and others negatively; as in 17:22–38, each form implies its opposite, such as monotheism from the ban on polytheism and kind treatment from the duty to honor parents.
rows.anchor: Exactly the same style has been adopted in these directives in verses 22-38 of Sūrah Banī Isrā’īl.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The positive command to treat parents kindly tacitly forbids disrespect and scolding; 17:23–24 makes those implications explicit and adds tender speech and humility.
rows.anchor: disrespect to the parents nor scold them; in fact, be kind to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imlāq means poverty; fear of feeding and raising children must not lead to killing them, which occurred through idolatrous custom, female infanticide tied to honor, and poverty.
rows.anchor: means “poverty.” In verse 31 of Sūrah Banī Isrā’īl

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parents are custodians, not providers: God sustains both them and their children, so they must fulfill their duties to children according to reason and religion.
rows.anchor: It is God Who not only provides the children but also the parents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Governments can overstep by entering God's domain, thereby acting against nature and their creator instead of benefiting citizens.
rows.anchor: instead of being beneficial to their citizens, they end up fighting against nature and their creator.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A conscientious government should develop livelihoods and educate people toward moderation and diligence, but must not impose a population quota or prevent births through birth control.
rows.anchor: it would be exceeding limits if a government starts ordering them to produce a certain amount of children

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Modern family planning repeats the Jāhiliyyah rationale for killing children: both assume people themselves provide sustenance and resent God's provision of children.
rows.anchor: The philosophy of both is the same: both regard themselves to be the providers of sustenance.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vice can only be removed when it is uprooted from the heart.
rows.anchor: cannot be gotten rid of unless it is uprooted from the heart.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vice nourished through the senses and thoughts grows into a spiritual cancer.
rows.anchor: it will continue to be nurtured through the eye, the ear, the tongue and thoughts until it becomes a spiritual cancer.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even unacted vice can grip the mind and heart so strongly that efforts at self-cleansing fail.
rows.anchor: Even if it may never materialize practically, it grips the mind and heart of a person

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Virtue and vice originate in the heart; vice sustained by the senses and thoughts can become spiritual cancer even without outward action, so believers must avoid inner and outer lewdness.
rows.anchor: inner and outer forms of lewdness.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every soul is sacred; killing is permitted under the Sharīʿah only for offenses such as murder, rebellion against God and His messenger, or adultery, and otherwise is unjustified.
rows.anchor: Without such offences, killing someone is not justified.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh abandoned Abraham's directives while claiming his religion through food taboos; the Prophet recounts them so they reconsider and understand their deviation.
rows.anchor: the Quraysh have abandoned them and by regarding some lawful animals to be unlawful, they claim to be followers of this religion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphan wealth must be approached only for the orphan's benefit, managed and increased, then returned at maturity in the presence of witnesses.
rows.anchor: The only proper way to go near their wealth is to manage it and further enhance it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The positive command to give full measure implies its opposite is forbidden; 83:1–3 condemns short measure.
rows.anchor: Woe be to those who weigh and measure less!

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe rests on justice; honest measure supports a just economy, while dishonest dealings prevent development, spread disorder, and bring a nation's destruction under God's established practice.
rows.anchor: Nations which are dishonest in their dealings have never developed in this world nor is their any chance for them to do so.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's commands fit human capacity and inadvertent mistakes are overlooked; the verse also rejects both excessive caution and the claim that individuals may set their own limit of obedience.
rows.anchor: Nothing among them are beyond their capacity and capability. Secondly, everyone must follow these directives with full honesty and veracity

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speaking truth even about relatives is general, but here specifically requires truthful testimony and decisions regardless of kinship; 17:36 also prohibits claiming what one does not know.
rows.anchor: no evidence borne and no decision given by people should be against the truth even if the matter relates to their relatives.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulfilling God's promise includes His covenants and people's promises to one another for noble causes; every promise within God's limits makes its keeper accountable to God.
rows.anchor: This includes promises which God has taken from people as well as those which they make with one another for any noble cause.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence moves from reflection that frees one from blind following, to recalling truths of human nature, then to taqwā; Sharīʿah's fundamentals emerge from human nature when people heed God's reminder.
rows.anchor: The sharī‘ah is a treasury that has been extracted from our nature and has been consigned to us

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, mustaqīman is an accusative of state governed by the verb in the demonstrative expression.
rows.anchor: is an accusative of state. The verb found in the demonstrative noun is acting on it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path presented by the Prophet is God's instruction and Abraham's teaching; abandoning other paths prevents deviation and punishment.
rows.anchor: the straight path which the Prophet (sws) is presenting before them should be followed by them; it is instructed by God and taught by Abraham (sws) to his progeny.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as wholesome purity distinguishes lawful food, justice, goodness, and good conventions distinguish commanded conduct from rebellion, lewdness, and vice in Abraham's and Islam's religions.
rows.anchor: all things that are enjoined stem from justice, goodness and good conventions and all things that are forbidden stem from rebelliousness, lewdness and vice.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses' first directives on tablets are famously known as the Ten Commandments.
rows.anchor: The first directives given to Moses (sws) written on tablets are famously known as the “Ten Commandments.”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ten Commandments given to Moses share Abraham's religious essentials and were also given to this community; religion is one, while details and completion differ, and the final Sharīʿah removes restrictions imposed on Jews for rebellion.
rows.anchor: In other words, actual religion is one. Difference lies only in details and completion.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against the view that tamāman ʿalā alladhī aḥsana refers to a group, Islahi prefers Moses: the singular relative pronoun conventionally refers to a person here.
rows.anchor: However, in my opinion, they refer to Moses (sws).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was thorough in fulfilling God's favors and duties, which made him worthy of further favor and messengerhood; the contrast reminds Jews of their ingratitude and distortion.
rows.anchor: He was thorough in his deeds. He understood his obligation to the favours God bestowed on him intrinsically and extrinsically

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “An explanation of everything” means the full details and corollaries of religion; scripture guides earthly life so people may receive mercy in the afterlife and believe in meeting their Lord.
rows.anchor: They are revealed so that they guide people to the way according to which they should lead their lives in this world which will then earn them His mercy in the next world.
